extracted.intended_audience: ETSI members, SEP owners/declarants, implementers of ETSI standards, and other stakeholders involved in standardisation and patent licensing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for declaring Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) to ETSI, the licensing commitment expected (FRAND), use of the ETSI IPR database, and related copyright/antitrust obligations when contributing to or implementing ETSI standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAND licensing commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Policy based on Fair, Reasonable And Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) licensing commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPR policy balances standardisation needs for public use with rights of IPR owners. The double-objective is to: (1) encourage IPR owners to submit their most innovative technologies and be fairly rewarded for use of their SEPs; and (2) enable implementers of ETSI standards to have access to such technologies under FRAND conditions. ETSI's basic principle remains FRAND with no specific preference for any licensing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely disclosure obligation for ETSI members
rubrics_metrics.description: During the proposal or development of a standard, ETSI members must inform the Director General in a timely fashion if they are aware that they hold any patent that might be essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is expected during proposal/development phases so ETSI and participants can consider potential SEPs; members use the ETSI IPR database to record such patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP disclosure by other stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Other stakeholders may use the same procedure to disclose their SEPs in the ETSI IPR database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-members are permitted to disclose patents via the online disclosure process; the database is the central public repository for declared essential or potentially essential patents to ETSI and 3GPP standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrevocable undertaking to grant licenses on FRAND terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Standard Essential Patents (SEP) holders are requested to provide an irrevocable undertaking in writing that they are prepared to grant irrevocable licenses on Fair, Reasonable And Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarants are expected to supply an irrevocable written undertaking as part of their disclosure; prior to making a patent licensing decision and implementing any SEP contained in the ETSI IPR Database, potential licensees shall always contact the declarant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for potential licensees to contact declarant
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a patent licensing decision and implementing any SEP contained in the ETSI IPR Database, potential licensees shall always contact the declarant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the declarant is mandatory practice before implementing or making licensing decisions based on database entries; licensing terms and negotiations remain commercial matters between companies and are not addressed within ETSI.

rubrics_metrics.name: ETSI IPR online database practices (normalised vs un-normalised numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalised patent numbers are imported from the European Patent Office (EPO) Espacenet database and appear in black; un-normalised patent numbers do not match Espacenet and are created manually and appear in purple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalised numbers link directly to EPO Espacenet allowing access to patent information. Un-normalised numbers may be correct but are not checked and lack links to Espacenet; the colour-coding helps users distinguish the data type. Declarants are encouraged to update un-normalised disclosures when EPO data becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database tools: bulk upload and update features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulk upload feature enables users to upload large amounts of SEPs in one file; the update tool enables users to update their un-normalised SEPs in reflected declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools are provided to optimise time and to allow declarants to normalise/update records when additional patent-related information becomes available (e.g., reflected in EPO databases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership of ETSI standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The ownership of the copyright in standards created by ETSI or any of its committees shall vest in ETSI; ETSI is responsible for the copyright management having all rights reserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards are publicly available for consultation from ETSI's Standards section. Reproduction of parts of ETSI standards may be allowed provided a request is made using the ETSI Copyright Licence request form. Copyright authorisation shall never imply a license on any potential SEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software contributions: copyright licence terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where software is included in any element of an ETSI standard, the software owner grants, without monetary compensation an irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free and sub-licensable copyright license to prepare derivative works and reproduce, display, distribute and execute the contributed software and derivative work to ETSI, ETSI members and any implementer for limited purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software contribution licensing is governed by Section 9.2 of the ETSI Directives; the copyright license granted for contributed software is distinct from any patent/SEP licensing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust / competition law compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: ETSI’s position as a recognised European Standards Organisation does not exempt ETSI nor its members from the application of competition law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidelines on how to ensure compliance with relevant laws on antitrust are part of the ETSI Directives. For further information, contact the provided ETSI antitrust email.

rubrics_metrics.name: ETSI neutrality on interpretation and licensing negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: ETSI does not take any position regarding the correct interpretation of its IPR policy and its IPR Guide; specific licensing terms and negotiations are commercial matters between the companies and shall not be addressed within ETSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ETSI issues a public statement clarifying that the IPR Policy and IPR Guide texts stand as independent documents; ETSI will not adjudicate licensing disputes or interpret policy texts for commercial negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and transparency of standards and declared patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The ETSI IPR online database provides public access for information to patents which were declared as being essential or potentially essential to ETSI and 3GPP standards; ETSI standards are publicly available for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public database and publication of standards support transparency for implementers and stakeholders; users should consult the database and standards pages and follow provided guides/eLearning for disclosure and database use.
